## Visa Guide for: Australia
**Applicable to:** Indian Passport Holders Only
**Last Updated Officially On:** April 2026 (13% Subclass 600 fee increase applied)
**Information Status:** Current as of August 29, 2026

---

## Overview

### Country Information

-   **Country Name:** Australia
-   **Region:** Oceania
-   **Capital:** Canberra
-   **Official Language:** English (no official language at federal level, but English is the language of government)
-   **Currency:** Australian Dollar (AUD)
-   **Exchange Rate:** 1 AUD = 68.3 INR (approximate)

> **Important:** Australia's two lightest-weight entry options — the **ETA (Subclass 601)** and **eVisitor (Subclass 651)** — are both restricted to specific passport lists that **do not include India**. There is no visa-on-arrival either. Every Indian passport holder, for any purpose, must apply for the full **Visitor visa (Subclass 600)** online through ImmiAccount. Be wary of agents who claim they can get Indians an eVisitor or ETA — this isn't possible, and any "approval" offered this way is fraudulent.

---

## Visa Type 1: Visitor Visa (Subclass 600) — Tourist Stream

### Overview

The standard route for Indian tourists, family visits, and casual sightseeing trips. Applied for entirely online via ImmiAccount — there's normally no in-person interview. If granted, the visa is fully electronic and linked to your passport (no sticker); border checks and any third-party verification (e.g., by an airline or employer) use the government's VEVO system. A case officer decides your permitted stay — 3, 6, or 12 months — based on your circumstances, with most first-time applicants receiving a shorter grant. The single biggest factor in approval is satisfying the "Genuine Temporary Entrant" (GTE) requirement — demonstrating a credible, temporary purpose and clear intent to return to India.

### Cost Structure

| Cost Component | Amount |
| :------------- | :----- |
| Visa Application Charge (Tourist Stream) | 190 AUD (~12,977 INR) — following an approximately 13% increase applied in April 2026 |
| **Total Cost** | **190 AUD (~12,977 INR)**, non-refundable regardless of outcome |

> **Note:** At least one source reports a further increase to AUD 250 effective 1 July 2026, while multiple sources dated as recently as mid-August 2026 still cite AUD 190 as current. This is worth double-checking on the official ImmiAccount fee estimator immediately before you apply, since Home Affairs fees have moved more than once through 2026.

### Mandatory Document Requirements (Type 1)

1.  **Passport Details**
    *   **Validity:** Should cover your intended stay, with some buffer recommended.
2.  **Photograph (Digital)**
    *   Uploaded as part of the online ImmiAccount application.
3.  **Travel Proof**
    *   **Itinerary:** A clear, specific travel plan.
    *   **Accommodation:** Hotel bookings or an invitation letter if visiting family/friends.
4.  **Genuine Temporary Entrant (GTE) Evidence**
    *   The most scrutinized part of the application — evidence of strong ties to India (employment, property, family, business) and a credible reason the visit is genuinely temporary. Weak GTE evidence is the leading cause of refusal, well ahead of simple paperwork errors.
5.  **Financial Proof**
    *   Bank statements and income documentation showing sufficient funds for the trip without needing to work in Australia.
6.  **Health & Character:** Some applicants (depending on intended stay length and personal circumstances) may be asked for a health examination or police clearance certificate (PCC) — not required for every applicant, but build in time if requested.

**Processing Time:** Reported ranges vary by source and season — commonly cited as roughly 15-33 days, with Home Affairs statistics suggesting about 75% of applications are decided within 20-24 days and up to 90% within 52 days. Peak periods (June-August, November-January) can extend this to 30-60 days. There is no official expedited/priority processing for the Tourist stream — apply 6-8 weeks ahead of your intended travel date.

---

## Visa Type 2: Visitor Visa (Subclass 600) — Business Visitor & Sponsored Family Streams

### Overview

Two other streams under the same Subclass 600 visa. The **Business Visitor stream** covers short-term business activities — meetings, conferences, exploring commercial opportunities — but explicitly does not permit paid employment or ongoing work for an Australian entity. The **Sponsored Family stream** is for visiting family already in Australia, where the Australian-resident family member acts as a sponsor and provides additional supporting documentation and, in some cases, a bond.

### Cost Structure

| Cost Component | Amount |
| :------------- | :----- |
| Visa Application Charge (Business Visitor Stream) | 190 AUD (~12,977 INR), same base fee as the Tourist stream |
| Visa Application Charge (Sponsored Family Stream) | 190 AUD base fee, though total costs can run higher with sponsorship and bond requirements |
| **Total Cost** | **190 AUD (~12,977 INR)** base fee for either stream |

### Mandatory Document Requirements (Type 2)

1.  **Business Visitor Stream**
    *   Invitation letter from the Australian host company, and a letter from your own employer confirming your role, salary, and approved leave for the trip.
2.  **Sponsored Family Stream**
    *   A completed sponsorship form from your Australian-based family member, evidence of the family relationship, and the sponsor's own proof of status (citizenship/PR) in Australia. This stream can also require a financial bond, refundable if you comply with your visa conditions.
3.  **Standard Documents**
    *   Same passport, GTE, and financial proof requirements as Type 1.

**Processing Time:** The Business Visitor stream is generally faster (commonly cited around 7-14 days), while the Sponsored Family stream is often slower and more variable (some estimates run into several weeks, occasionally longer given the added sponsorship verification).

---

## Visa Type 3: Student Visa (Subclass 500) & Other Long-Term Categories

### Overview

For Indian students admitted to an Australian institution, this is the relevant long-term category, distinct from the short-stay Subclass 600. Australia remains one of the top destinations for Indian students, and — under the Australia-India Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (AIFTA) — eligible graduates in select fields can access post-study work rights of up to 8 years, a notably longer window than many other study-destination countries offer.

### Cost Structure

| Cost Component | Amount |
| :------------- | :----- |
| Student Visa (Subclass 500) Base Fee | From approximately 2,000 AUD (~1,36,600 INR) |
| **Total Cost** | **Varies by course level and duration — starts around 2,000 AUD** |

### Mandatory Document Requirements (Type 3)

1.  **Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)**
    *   Issued by the Australian institution once you've accepted your offer and paid the required deposit/fees.
2.  **Financial Capacity**
    *   Evidence of funds covering tuition, living costs, and travel for the duration of the course, per Home Affairs' published thresholds.
3.  **Genuine Student (GS) Requirement**
    *   Similar in spirit to the GTE test for visitor visas — evidence that your study plan is credible and genuinely your primary purpose.
4.  **Health & Character**
    *   Health examination and police clearance certificate (PCC) are standard requirements for student visa categories.

---

## Special Cases & Exemptions

-   **India Is Not Eligible for ETA or eVisitor:** Worth repeating plainly — the ETA (Subclass 601) is available to only about 9 passport lists (including the US, Canada, Singapore, Japan, South Korea), and the eVisitor (Subclass 651) is for European passport holders. India is on neither, and there are no current bilateral discussions to add it.
-   **Transit Through Australia Requires Its Own Visa:** This catches many Indian travelers off guard — because Indians can't use the ETA/eVisitor, even a layover through an Australian airport (for example, en route to New Zealand or a Pacific island) generally requires a **Transit visa (Subclass 771)**, not just a boarding pass. Check your specific routing and layover length with your airline or the Australian High Commission before assuming you can transit visa-free.
-   **OCI Cardholders with a Foreign Passport:** If you hold an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card alongside an eligible foreign passport (e.g., UK, Canada, or US for ETA purposes), you would apply using that foreign passport's rules instead — the OCI card itself gives no separate Australian visa concession, and this guide's advice applies specifically to those traveling on an Indian passport.
-   **No Refunds:** The visa application charge is non-refundable regardless of the outcome — factor this into your planning rather than treating it as a guaranteed-success fee.

---

## Arrival Documentation

-   **Electronic Visa, No Sticker:** Your Subclass 600 (or other) visa is linked electronically to your passport — there's no physical stamp or sticker to check, but you should still read your official grant letter carefully for your exact permitted stay length and any conditions.
-   **VEVO (Visa Entitlement Verification Online):** Australia's system for confirming visa details — airlines and immigration use this to verify your status; you can also check your own visa conditions here before traveling.
-   **Return/Onward Ticket & Accommodation Proof:** Keep evidence accessible, as immigration officers may ask about your travel plans again on arrival even after visa approval.

---

## Comparison Table

| Feature | Visitor Visa — Tourist Stream | Visitor Visa — Business/Sponsored Family | Student Visa (Subclass 500) |
| :-------------------- | :-------------------- | :------------------------- | :---------------------------------- |
| **Total Cost** | 190 AUD (~12,977 INR) | 190 AUD (~12,977 INR) base | From ~2,000 AUD (~1,36,600 INR) |
| **Stay Duration** | 3, 6, or 12 months, case officer's discretion | Similar, tied to purpose | Duration of the enrolled course |
| **Where to Apply** | Online via ImmiAccount | Online via ImmiAccount | Online via ImmiAccount, after receiving a CoE |
| **Advance Planning** | Moderate-High — apply 6-8 weeks ahead given variable processing | Similar to Tourist stream | Extensive — CoE and financial documentation take time to assemble |
| **Best For** | Tourism, casual family/friend visits | Short-term business trips, family sponsorship visits | Students pursuing an Australian qualification |

---

**Disclaimer:** This guide provides general information for Indian passport holders. Always verify current requirements and the exact fee on the official Department of Home Affairs website (immi.homeaffairs.gov.au) and ImmiAccount before applying, as Subclass 600 fees have changed more than once through 2026, and processing times fluctuate significantly with application volume and season.
